chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who prayed in congregation on the day of al-Jumuʿah: when the Imam bowed, the people pressed him against a wall or a pillar, so he was unable to bow or to prostrate until the people raised their heads. Should he bow, then prostrate, and join the row after the people have stood, or how should he act?
So he said: “He should bow and prostrate, then stand in the row, and there is no harm in that.”

key_terms.رَكَعَ: performed rukuʿ, the bowing position in salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.يَسْجُدَ: perform sajdah, the prostration in salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, in the context of Jumuʿah prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in Jumuʿah prayer if the crowd prevents him from bowing and prostrating with the congregation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one praying in congregation on Friday who is physically prevented by the crowd from performing rukuʿ and sajdah at their proper moment. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to perform the missed bowing and prostration afterward and then rejoin the row, affirming that there is no problem in doing so.
